machine: Each experiment runs on a single CPU thread

hyperparameters: Deep Ensemble classifier with a simple architecture: 4 fully connected layers with 64*floor(log2(d)) neurons per hidden layer
Optimized using variational inference (ELBO) rather than maximum likelihood
Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 3e-4
random_seed: Experiments run with 10 different random seeds using the same initial Sobol sequence

metrics_used: Current best objective value (f′) over evaluations
Feasibility ratio (ratio of feasible to total points)
statistical_results: Mean and standard deviation computed over 10 random seeds
figure_results: Figures 3, 4, and 5 display quantitative and qualitative performance comparisons

Expected Results: BE-CBO consistently exhibits top performance with low variance across both synthetic and real-world benchmarks
It effectively explores the boundary between feasible and infeasible regions to accurately identify the global optimum
Deep Ensembles yield more robust constraint modeling than Gaussian Processes, especially in high-dimensional problems
Although very robust overall, BE-CBO is slightly outperformed by SCBO in the 30D cantilever beam design case
Notes: Experiments use 10 initial random samples and 200 total evaluations per run
The dynamic bound strategy adapts based on classifier uncertainty
All experiments are conducted in parallel on a distributed server with single-threaded CPU jobs
